phrases.translation: By the dawn
phrases.text: God swears by the dawn, and by the dawn He means the early morning light. The commentators differed: some took it as the day itself, some as the morning prayer, and some as the dawn of the morning.

phrases.translation: and the ten nights
phrases.text: The commentators differed about which ten nights are meant: the ten nights of Dhū al-Hijjah, or the ten days of the festival of sacrifice. Tabari holds the days of the festival, because the authorities agreed on it and the Prophet said the same.

phrases.translation: and the even and the odd
phrases.text: The commentators differed: some said the even is the day of sacrifice and the odd the day of Arafah, others the two days after the sacrifice and the day of departure, and others that all creation is the even and God alone is the odd.

phrases.translation: and the night when it passes
phrases.text: God swears by the night as it passes away. Some said this is the night of the gathering at Muzdalifah. As for the reading of the word, most reciters leave out the letter yā, and Tabari prefers that, because it matches the rhymes of the passage.

phrases.translation: Is all this ˹not˺ a sufficient oath for those who have sense
phrases.text: Is this oath enough for anyone with understanding? The commentators explain those with understanding as people with discernment and sound mind, and Tabari adds that it also means the person who holds himself back and governs his passions.
phrases.ar: هَلۡ فِي ذَٰلِكَ قَسَمٞ لِّذِي حِجۡرٍ

phrases.translation: Did you not see how your Lord dealt with ’Ȃd—
phrases.text: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, how your Lord dealt with the people of Ad, who were tall as palm trunks and whose like was never created again?
phrases.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ

phrases.translation: ˹the people˺ of Iram—with ˹their˺ great stature
phrases.text: The commentators differed about Iram: some said it is a city, some a tribe of Ad, and some that it means an ancient people. For the pillars, some said they were tall in body, some that they were tent-dwellers, and some that they built a structure with high pillars. Tabari takes the tent-pole sense.

phrases.translation: unmatched in any other land
phrases.text: The like of them was never created in the lands, in size, in violence and in strength. Some said they were twelve cubits tall, measured heavenward.
phrases.ar: ٱلَّتِي لَمۡ يُخۡلَقۡ مِثۡلُهَا فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ

phrases.translation: and Thamûd who carved ˹their homes into˺ the rocks in the ˹Stone˺ Valley
phrases.text: And Thamud, the people of Salih, who cut into the rock and made dwellings of it, so that they lived in safety in the mountains.

phrases.translation: and the Pharaoh of mighty structures
phrases.text: And Pharaoh, the lord of the stakes. The commentators differed: some said the stakes are his armies, some that he used them to torture people, and some that they were the canopies and playing grounds before which people amused themselves. Tabari takes the stakes, of wood or iron, by which he tortured them.

phrases.translation: They all transgressed throughout the land
phrases.text: Those who means Ad and Thamud and Pharaoh and his army. Transgressed means they exceeded what their Lord allowed them and rose against Him toward what He forbade them, which is disbelief in Him.

phrases.translation: spreading much corruption there
phrases.text: And they increased in the lands in disobedience and in doing what God had forbidden them.

phrases.translation: So your Lord unleashed on them a scourge of punishment
phrases.text: Your Lord sent His punishment down on them and took His revenge, because of the corruption they worked on the earth. What came down on them were visitations of punishment, a wind that destroyed them, an earthquake that buried them, or a flood that swallowed them, without any blow of a whip.

phrases.translation: ˹For˺ your Lord is truly vigilant
phrases.text: Your Lord lies in wait for those whose story has been told you and for their like among the unbelievers, watching them on the bridges of Hell so that He may gather them there. Some said it means a place where He sees and hears, and some said it means the place of the reckoning.

phrases.translation: Now, whenever a human being is tested by their Lord through ˹His˺ generosity and blessings, they boast, “My Lord has ˹deservedly˺ honoured me!”
phrases.text: When God tests a person with favours and wealth, giving him possessions and making his life easy, the person rejoices in it and says: my Lord has honoured me. He is thanking his Lord for the gift and forgetting the One who gave it.
phrases.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكۡرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَكۡرَمَنِ

phrases.translation: But when He tests them by limiting their provision, they protest, “My Lord has ˹undeservedly˺ humiliated me!”
phrases.text: But when God tests a person with poverty and narrows his provision, the person says: my Lord has humiliated me. He does not give thanks for the sound limbs and the well-being of his body, and Qatada says: how quickly the son of Adam turns to ingratitude.
phrases.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَهَٰنَنِ

phrases.translation: Absolutely not! In fact, you are not ˹even˺ gracious to the orphan
phrases.text: Never. God honours no one for the abundance of what he has and humiliates no one for its lack. He honours the one He honours with obedience to Him, and humiliates the one He humiliates with disobedience to Him, and He has told you why: you do not honour the orphan.

phrases.translation: nor do you urge one another to feed the poor
phrases.text: And you do not urge one another to feed the needy. The reciters differ on the wording here, but Tabari holds that all three well-known readings carry a sound meaning, so the reciter is right whichever of them he uses.

phrases.translation: And you devour ˹others’˺ inheritance greedily
phrases.text: You devour the inheritance with a ravenous greed that leaves nothing behind. Some said that means you take your own share and your companion's share, and Ibn Zayd adds that they used to let neither the women nor the small children inherit at all.

phrases.translation: and love wealth fervently
phrases.text: You love to gather and to possess wealth with a great and intense love. The commentators agree that the word means intense or abundant love of wealth.

phrases.translation: Enough! When the earth is entirely crushed over and over
phrases.text: Never. God then gives tidings of their regret over what they did in the world, when the regret will avail them nothing. The earth is crushed, that is, it is shaken and convulsed and set in motion, motion upon motion.
phrases.ar: كـَلَّآۖ إِذَا دُكَّتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ دَكّٗا دَكّٗا

phrases.translation: and your Lord comes ˹to judge˺ with angels, rank upon rank
phrases.text: Your Lord comes on the day of resurrection, and the angels come in rows, one row after another. The earth is spread out, heaven after heaven is broken down onto it, and the communities kneel in rows while a herald calls out to those who praised God in every state.

phrases.translation: and Hell is brought forth on that Day—this is when every ˹disbelieving˺ person will remember ˹their own sins˺. But what is the use of remembering then
phrases.text: Hell is brought forth that day, dragged along by seventy thousand reins with seventy thousand angels on each rein. On that day man remembers how he neglected obeying God and the good deeds he left undone. But how can remembering help him then?
phrases.ar: وَجِاْيٓءَ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِجَهَنَّمَۚ يَوۡمَئِذٖ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ

phrases.translation: They will cry, “I wish I had sent forth ˹something good˺ for my ˹true˺ life.”
phrases.text: They will say: would that I had sent forward good deeds in this life of mine, deeds that would have won me the pleasure of God and saved me from His anger. The life they mean is the long life that never ends.

phrases.translation: On that Day He will punish ˹them˺ severely, like no other
phrases.text: On that day no one will punish as God punishes, and no one will bind as He binds. God said this because there is punishment and binding in this world, and on that day His punishment and His binding are beyond anything else.

phrases.translation: and bind ˹them˺ tightly, like no other
phrases.text: And no one will bind as He binds. The correct reading, in Tabari's judgment, is the one the reciters of the regions agree on, and the meaning is that nothing in this world can equal His punishment and His binding on that day.

phrases.translation: ˹Allah will say to the righteous,˺ “O tranquil soul
phrases.text: The angels say to the believers on the day of resurrection: O you tranquil soul. The tranquil one is she who was calm at God's promise of the honour of the hereafter, and who believed it true. Some said the words are spoken to the soul as it leaves the body at death.

phrases.translation: Return to your Lord, well pleased ˹with Him˺ and well pleasing ˹to Him˺
phrases.text: Return to your Lord, well pleased with Him and well pleasing to Him. Some said this is said at death, and some that it is said on the day of resurrection when the souls are returned to the bodies. Tabari keeps the latter, because of what follows.

phrases.translation: So join My servants
phrases.text: Then enter among My servants. The commentators said this means among My righteous servants. Tabari notes that the saying belongs to the day of resurrection, when the spirits return to the bodies.

phrases.translation: and enter My Paradise.”
phrases.text: And enter My Paradise. Some said this means enter My obedience and My mercy, and some that it means My retinue, but the correct reading is the one all the reciters agree on.
